title: ESTRO Signs Joint Statement on AI-Enabled Medical Technologies Regulation
key_facts: The European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology (ESTRO) shared the statement on LinkedIn.

ESTRO has joined MedTech Europe and partner healthcare organisations in signing a joint statement on the ongoing revision of the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and In Vitro Diagnostics Regulation (IVDR).
ESTRO supports a streamlined, single regulatory pathway that builds AI Act requirements directly into MDR/IVDR.
It says this avoids double regulation, keeps safety standards high and speeds patient access to AI innovation.
ESTRO says AI holds potential in radiation oncology: earlier diagnosis, more personalised treatment, better clinical decisions.
quote_evidence: ESTRO has joined MedTech Europe and partner healthcare organisations in signing a joint statement regarding the ongoing revision of the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and In Vitro Diagnostics Regulation (IVDR).
This approach avoids double regulation, ensures high safety standards, and accelerates patient access to essential AI innovation.
why_it_matters_hint: A medical society wants one set of EU rules for AI medical devices instead of two.
event_date: Post dated 16 Oct 2026; signing date not stated.
notes: Oncodaily reproduces ESTRO's own LinkedIn post, so ESTRO is credited. The joint statement itself and its other signatories were not found.
